key_insight: An unsupervised Cycle-GAN–style framework augmented with a Perceptual Attention Network can denoise real clinical low‑dose liver CT scans, removing noise while preserving anatomical detail without requiring paired high‑dose references.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of paired low-/high-dose clinical CT data by enabling effective denoising of low‑dose liver CT images in an unsupervised manner, reducing noise and artifacts that can impair diagnosis.
method: Cycle-consistent adversarial training to learn mappings between low‑dose and clean domains using unpaired clinical data.
Perceptual Attention Network that applies spatial attention and perceptual losses to prioritize clinically relevant liver structures and preserve edges/textures.
End‑to‑end training on real clinical scans (no paired labels), combining adversarial, cycle, and perceptual objectives to balance noise suppression and detail preservation.
impact: Makes clinically viable CT denoising possible where paired datasets are unavailable, helping ML practitioners build robust, annotation‑free restoration pipelines that maintain diagnostic information in low‑dose imaging.
visual_elements: Before / after CT slice triptych: low‑dose input, denoised output, (optional) standard reference
Model architecture diagram showing Cycle‑GAN backbone with the Perceptual Attention module highlighted
Attention heatmaps overlaid on liver regions to illustrate where the network focuses during denoising
Compact charts comparing image‑quality metrics and a short qualitative reader assessment (e.g., perceived noise vs. detail)
paper_title: Unsupervised Denoising of Real Clinical Low Dose Liver CT with Perceptual Attention Networks
paper_authors: Jingxi Pu, Tonghua Liu, Zhilin Guan, Siqiao Li, Yang Ming
